edges.description: Loss of Tuba-dependent Cdc42 activation at the apical junction alters junctional F-actin and E-cadherin assembly.

Proposed link: E-cadherin is needed for lens vesicle separation and lens epithelial cell survival, so disordered junctional E-cadherin is expected to compromise lens development. Not demonstrated in a vertebrate lens.
Knockdown disrupts development of lens-secreting cells, E-cadherin localization and septate junction distribution, and halves electroretinogram amplitudes in young flies.
edges.limitations: The insect compound-eye lens is a secreted cuticular structure, not a cellular lens built from crystallin-filled fiber cells, and septate junctions are only functional counterparts of vertebrate tight junctions. The model shows a junctional defect, not lens opacity.

nodes.description: All pathogenic alleles reported so far are homozygous nonsense or frameshift variants (p.Arg271*, p.Asp983*, p.Thr951Metfs*41, p.Arg640*) predicted to abolish Tuba, including its central Dbl homology domain, which activates Cdc42 but not Rac or Rho.

evidence.snippet: Using exome sequencing, we found homozygous loss-of-function variants in DNMBP: nonsense variant c.811C>T (p.Arg271∗) in large family F385 (nine affected individuals; LOD score = 5.18 at θ = 0), frameshift deletion c.2947_2948del (p.Asp983∗) in family F372 (two affected individuals), and frameshift variant c.2852_2855del (p.Thr951Metfs∗41) in family F3 (one affected individual).

evidence.reference_title: Tuba, a novel protein containing bin/amphiphysin/Rvs and Dbl homology domains, links dynamin to regulation of the actin cytoskeleton.
evidence.snippet: A Dbl homology domain present in the middle of Tuba upstream of a Bin/amphiphysin/Rvs (BAR) domain activates Cdc42, but not Rac and Rho, and may thus cooperate with the C terminus of the protein in regulating actin assembly.

nodes.description: In cultured epithelia Tuba depletion leaves cell junctions curved and slack and alters E-cadherin assembly; in the fly eye, knockdown of the ortholog sif disrupts E-cadherin localization in lens-secreting cells and septate junction distribution in neighbouring cone cells. Lens epithelial cells are bound here as the presumed affected cell type in human cataract; no study has examined junctions in a DNMBP-deficient vertebrate lens.

evidence.reference_title: Bi-allelic Loss-of-Function Variants in DNMBP Cause Infantile Cataracts.
evidence.snippet: RNAi-mediated knockdown of the Drosophila ortholog still life (sif), enriched in lens-secreting cells, affects the development of these cells as well as the localization of E-cadherin, alters the distribution of septate junctions in adjacent cone cells, and leads to a ∼50% reduction in electroretinography amplitudes in young flies.
